A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Streamo research and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-C. Content can be matched reliably despite extensive reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original Streamo evaluations on streaming and offline video benchmarks, loss ablations, and additional backbone experiments in the appendix.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds Streamo results on ViSpeak-Bench and an EOS-only training ablation.

M1.justification: The multi-turn formulation, Silence/Standby/Response states, frequency-balanced focal objective, and data-generation pipeline remain unchanged. V2 introduces EOS-only training as an ablation comparator, not a replacement for the proposed method.

E1.justification: V2 adds evaluation on ViSpeak-Bench, extending coverage to another corpus of streaming visual-instruction responses (Appendix A.3, Table 8). The training sources, existing streaming benchmarks, and four offline benchmarks are retained; this is a bounded extension within the same research domain.

E2.justification: V2 adds ViSpeak-7B to the OVO-Bench comparison, where it was absent from v1. The new ViSpeak-Bench table also introduces InternVL-2.5, VITA 1.5, and Ola into the reported comparisons, and Table 7 adds an EOS-only control. Comparator membership in the other retained experiments is unchanged.

E3.justification: V2 introduces a comparison holding Streamo-Instruct training data fixed while replacing the three-state design with EOS-only training. Its ViSpeak-Bench evaluation reports time accuracy, text scores, and an overall score for Streamo-7B at 1 fps. Existing training settings and Streamo-Bench metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's loss ablations and instruction-following examples, v2 adds a focused test of three-state versus EOS-only training on OVO-Bench and forward grounding (A.5, Table 7). New Figure 4 illustrates state transitions during pole-vault QA and grounding. Earlier analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports model seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added results remain point estimates; the human average/maximum rows in Table 8 are comparator summaries rather than uncertainty estimates for Streamo.

E6.justification: All retained result values are unchanged, but new evidence materially changes the central online ranking: ViSpeak-7B scores 61.08 overall on OVO-Bench versus Streamo-7B's 55.61 at 1 fps. V2 also adds ViSpeak-Bench outcomes and the EOS ablation: three-state versus EOS-only training scores 52.33 versus 48.52 overall on OVO-Bench and 14.7 versus 9.3 on forward grounding. These are new comparisons, not improvements in retained Streamo scores across versions.

T1.justification: Equations 1-17 retain the same streaming formulation, loss definitions, and evaluation mathematics. The new three-state discussion supplies an intuitive mechanism explanation, without new formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about unified streaming training, Streamo-Instruct-465K, Streamo-Bench, and broad performance. The added evidence does not redefine these contributions or narrow the existing superiority claims.

C2.justification: New Appendix A.5 attributes EOS-only failures to conflating irrelevant and partially relevant frames, arguing that Standby preserves attention and fuller event coverage. A.3 interprets ViSpeak-Bench timing results as support for the response architecture. Existing limitations concerning unbounded context, memory, and latency are unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 newly specifies Streamo-Bench's per-video allocation: two grounding tasks, one dense-caption task, one narration task, and remaining TSQA tasks (C.1). It removes v1's direct code and dataset links while retaining the project link. These are documentation and access-information changes; existing prompts and hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds references for ViSpeak, InternVL-2.5, VITA-1.5, and Ola alongside the expanded comparisons. The existing related-work discussion and overall research positioning remain substantially unchanged; citation renumbering is merely editorial.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section order are retained. Local changes include expanding and renaming Appendix A.3, adding A.5's explanation, clarifying benchmark task allocation, adding an acknowledgement, and correcting the dialogue-example cross-reference. These do not constitute a broad narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: V2 replaces the branded single-column presentation with a two-column conference layout, substantially changing typography, headings, abstract presentation, and display placement throughout. It adds Tables 7-8 and the decoding visualization in Figure 4, and relabels v1's dialogue-format Figure 2 as Table 1. Existing displays are extensively resized and repositioned.

improvement.justification: The new controlled EOS ablation supplies missing evidence for the three-state design, while ViSpeak-Bench broadens the empirical assessment. These provide a limited net gain in scientific support. However, Section 5.4 retains its SOTA superiority claim despite the added ViSpeak-7B row outperforming Streamo on OVO-Bench, and direct code/data links disappear. These shortcomings limit the improvement rather than supporting a substantial overall gain.
